comments.text: Started raining and there was no cover but everyone going down there will be going to the very outskirts of the city like cikampek or further, so it’s super quick to get picked up. It’s just wide enough for two trucks, so if one pulls over u gotta run/communicate quickly
Solo guy caucasian. Hitchhiked there for less than 10 minutes with a sign « Cikampek ». Great spot to get out of Jakarta heading to the east, good luck ✌🏻

comments.text:
We walked from city center to here. It was only 1,5km from our hotel. This is the best spot as it is the exit to every road going towards Ruteng. 

It took us 15 minutes to hop on the back of a truck and we went straight from Labuan Bajo to Ruteng.

Be aware that many cars and mini vans will stop to offer you a shared taxi service. That is how it works for locals, they “hitchhike” and pay what the driver ask. So just have your google translator ready with the explanation. 

The road was go

You can take angkot for 5k from the city to get to this place. Many small trucks are passing by, you can jump on one and get a lift in the back. We've changed 2 of them to reach Ruteng. Be aware, that minivans are mostly shared taxis. Make yourself clear before getting in.

comments.text: We got a direct ride to Jakarta from here. To get to this spot from the city take a yellow minibus "ampera — karya jaya", it's shown on the google maps as well, and it's correct. Say the driver you need simpang kramasan. The only thing that after 5 minutes of standing there, the annoying cop appeared and wanted us to leave from this turn to the main road. We didn't do it though and just walked down away from him a little, he only seemed confused. Gladly we got our ride after a few minutes.

In the end, the driver expected a payment from us. I had no problem paying him some money for the petrol, etc, but if you are not willing to pay make sure to figure it out beforehand.

I was there late at night and was lucky enough to be under a street lamp. Took an hour (and 11 rejections of a lift to a bus station/directions to a bus stop) to get a lift.

comments.text: It was the first time when we waited more than 10 minutes in Sumatra. Probably the spot wasn't good enough, cars were passing by too fast to break, so we had to change a few spots until we finally made it. To get to this junction from Padang Pajang you can simply take the small local minibus for 5000 rupiah (the one with an open door). We got a direct ride to Alahan Panjang (Danau Diatas), and the driver invited us to stay at his place.
